blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-reviewed 2026-10-19. The dominant deployment is Stellar token CDT3KU6TQZNOHKNOHNAFFDQZDURVC3MSTL4ML7TUTZGNOPBZCLABP4FR, whose instance PERM is the shared PermissionManager CBGHLRSX5D5YMBPNK4ZGMUTJUHFIT7YGXGJURM5LFNZ7B6WNSXLGS26M. Its transfer and safe_transfer methods require WHITELISTED_ROLE on both from and to, burn(account,amount,caller) burns an arbitrary account when called with BURNER_ROLE, pause is PAUSER_ROLE-gated and upgrade is owner-only. At Soroban ledger 65021030 (2026-10-19T06:22:13Z) simulateTransaction has_role returned WLISTER Some(0) for GD2ELXTHZQORSH75SJE6XRTCKXNDGJFIZ4R2SZ4MMXDOBT52GK26X4EO and Some(1) for GAUYO4UAESQD6SGZDPOIG2ADT7EZTR5EJ7HSX4CYCWS2JMMGQOCL4QCX, and BURNER Some(0) for redemption contract CAVZK26ERVGKGXLQGEOKPAQGIZS2YKN4BSXOYDMUY365EV66ZNSFEDBS; the permission-manager event history includes role_revoked|WLISTED, showing the issuer de-lists holders. EVM deployments use verified Spiko Token code: Token._update requires PermissionManager.canCall(from/to, token, 0xa9059cbb); restricted pause(), restricted burn(address,uint256) from an arbitrary holder and restricted UUPS upgrade are present. At Polygon block 95790196 (2026-10-19T06:17:21Z) authority 0x344278aff344d6fb960705dc18a4912221608472 returned getRequirements(token,0xa9059cbb)=65 and a holder-to-0x...0001 transfer reverted with UnauthorizedTo 0xb77a4ad1; group 0 is held by 3/3 Safe 0xa4196f06fe948b8ca81d3dc77110d3f83d10abd9. Arbitrum 0xa925C217e4c1C82Ee721eBD496d3863D5C2d829A (Safe 0x7843225ba488cf780a4fe2c842b5dc2abcf8a03e) and Ethereum 0x344278... (Safe 0x4eaa52b6280593a8820c45ce38f974290ae52cea) enforce the same requirement. Materiality: measured totalSupply at 2026-10-19 is 1,127,892,241,708 raw 5-decimal units: Stellar 921,188,198,315 (81.67%), Polygon 158,543,476,257 (14.06%), Arbitrum 41,965,066,272 (3.72%), Base 4,414,809,257 (0.39%), Starknet 931,108,610 (0.08%), Ethereum 849,582,997 (0.08%). Both material deployments are directly controlled. There is no declared parent; the reserve test is not reached because direct holder controls are established.

oracleRisk.summary: CACEIS Fund Administration originates the daily GBP fund NAV used for UKTBL subscriptions and redemptions. The exact UKTBL register binds GBP share class FR0014012MN7, and Spiko publishes its NAV through its public API. The issuer NAV provider table lists Spiko-operated UKTBL oracles on Polygon, Arbitrum, Base and Etherlink, with no UKTBL Ethereum Chainlink/RedStone entry; the Chainlink Ethereum feed directory searched on 25 October 2026 contains no UKTBL entry. This establishes privileged internal pricing, not an oracleless mechanism. No independent external UKTBL feed, redundancy, failover or publisher signer closure is credited.

Its own issuance mechanism has a top-level NAV authority, not borrower-specific liquidation branches. External lending integrations do not establish liquidation branches for this fund.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: UKTBL is natively issued by Spiko on all seven reviewed deployments. Chainlink CCIP BurnWithFromMintTokenPool 1.6.1 contracts on Ethereum, Polygon, Base, and Arbitrum provide the transfer rail's burn/mint return paths; their common EOA owner controls peer and rate-limit configuration. Etherlink has no current UKTBL CCIP pool. This supports the external-validated-network tier, while exact lane-by-lane remote-pool, OffRamp/RMN, rate-limit, pause, and upgrade observations remain pending.

controls.label: Chainlink CCIP UKTBL BurnWithFromMintTokenPool (Ethereum)

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: Chainlink CCIP OffRamp/source-pool validation and configured remote pools govern the burn/mint return path; exact lane-by-lane remote-pool and OffRamp/RMN observations remain pending.
routeChecks.rateLimits: Current per-lane CCIP rate-limit values were not captured; this pool's mint selector is a CCIP transfer-rail return path, not independent native issuance.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The pool's CCIP execution path can mint and burn local UKTBL; pool administration is attributed to the common owner EOA in the shared bridge control.

controls.capDescription: BurnWithFromMintTokenPool 1.6.1 provides CCIP burn/mint transfer-rail capability for the local Ethereum UKTBL; the pool is not a separate native-liability issuer.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770834, getToken() returned local UKTBL 0xf695df6c0f3bb45918a7a82e83348fc59517734e, typeAndVersion() returned BurnWithFromMintTokenPool 1.6.1, owner() returned 0xed608cf38968c0ba09676843d90b33dd59dd7375, and PermissionManager.canCall(pool, localUKTBL, mint) was true. CCIP burn/mint accounting and external validation make this bridge-route machinery rather than independent native issuance.

controls.label: Spiko UKTBL CCIP token-pool owner EOA

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: This common EOA owns the four reviewed pools and can change router and remote-pool configuration; exact lane-by-lane mappings and OffRamp/RMN state remain pending.
routeChecks.rateLimits: The common EOA can change chain rate-limiter configuration; current per-lane values were not captured.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: eth_getCode for the common owner returned 0x on Ethereum, Polygon, Base, and Arbitrum, so the controller is an EOA rather than a Safe.

controls.capDescription: Owner of the four identified UKTBL CCIP pools; can change router, remote-pool, and rate-limit configuration, so CCIP rate limits are not an immutable aggregate issuance cap.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770834, Polygon block 92144617, Base block 50066323, and Arbitrum block 495292872, the four UKTBL CCIP pools reported this common owner EOA. eth_getCode for the owner returned 0x on all four chains. The owner-controlled router, remote-pool, and chain-rate-limiter surfaces are bridge administration and remain scoreable here rather than in native Mint Authority.
